blocks.why: 06:10 report means leaving the door at 04:35 local, so lights out at 20:30 local tonight even if it feels early.
Straight to bed after the CDG day — the ARN report is 05:05 local and this is the only 7h30 on offer.
Two early starts back to back have left a debt; take 90 minutes when I get home rather than dragging through the afternoon.
Sleep in a bit for the ORD trip — I won't be in the hotel bed until nearly 01:30Z tomorrow.
An hour in the bank before a westbound that finishes at 01:05 body time, and I'm up a clear hour before I drive.
Bed as soon as I reach the hotel — it's the middle of my night even though Chicago says half eight in the evening.
Two hours before the redeye home so I'm not running on empty through the back of the clock; up 95 minutes before the crew bus.
Short top-up after the overnight, then stay up so I can get a proper night and be back on London time.
Full night to reset the body clock before the four-sector day that ends near midnight.
Home at 01:00 after BCN; sleep straight through and write off the morning.
Back onto a normal night before the ARN turn.
Normal night at home.
Day off — hold the same bedtime rather than drifting late, the 14th needs an 03:00 alarm.
Same anchor again ahead of the DUB afternoon.
Bed soon after getting in from DUB so tomorrow's early bedtime is achievable.
Lights out at 19:30 local for the 05:05 FRA report — dark room, no screens, this one is hard to get.
Eight hours banked the night before the JFK redeye, because tomorrow's duty runs right through my night.
Two hours in the afternoon before the JFK night sector, finished an hour before I leave so the fog has cleared.
Down as soon as I hit the hotel at 03:00 New York — I'm staying on London time for a one-night stop.
Ninety minutes before another all-nighter eastbound; up well before the pickup.
Two hours on landing from JFK, then up and about so tonight's sleep sticks.
Long night before SIN — that duty is planned at over fifteen hours and I want to start it topped up.
Blackout the room and sleep Singapore morning — it's my night, and I'm not shifting to +8 for two days.
Same London-time window again, right up against the 17:00 local pickup for the flight home.
Only six and a quarter hours here — the commute either side of a ten-hour rest leaves nothing more, see the conflict.
Second short night running; straight to bed on walking in, alarm at the last possible minute.
Long recovery night to pay back the two clipped nights before the day off.
Early to bed on the day off — the next three reports are all before 06:00 local.
Straight down after the FRA turn; no afternoon nap so I can actually fall asleep at 19:30 local.
Six hours and change after a thirteen-hour duty — this is the tightest night of the month, see the conflict.
Afternoon sleep as my main sleep before the FCO night duty — curtains shut, phone off, treat it like a night.
Six hours on getting home from the night flight, then up in the afternoon so I can sleep again tonight.
Proper night before the sim — the box is unforgiving when you're short.
Normal night after the sim.
Day off — full eight hours to clear the month's debt.
Last night of the period, back on a normal London night.

conflicts.statement: HY207 LHR-SIN is planned report 07:45Z to off-duty 23:05Z — 15h20 of flight duty against a 13h company ceiling. I cannot plan sleep inside the duty either, so nothing in this calendar offsets it.
options: Ask crewing to confirm this is a planned augmented FDP with an extension, and get the augmentation and in-flight rest allocation in writing before you go
Treat any in-flight rest as a tactical matter for the day, decided in the flight deck, not something you plan on now
If the pairing is not augmented, raise it with the operator before the roster is published as final

conflicts.statement: HY440 SIN-LHR is planned report 09:00Z to off-duty 00:20Z+1 — another 15h20 duty, and it ends into a minimum rest at home.
options: Same question to crewing on augmentation for the return sector
Take the second SIN sleep as late as possible (00:00Z-08:05Z as planned) so you start the duty on a full window
Flag the pairing plus the 21SEP turnaround together — it is the combination that bites, not either duty alone

conflicts.statement: Off duty 00:20Z after the SIN sector, report 10:20Z. That is exactly 10h00 rest, but 95 minutes of commute at each end leaves 6h50 of sleep opportunity, not 8h.
options: Notify the operator under 117.25(f) that this rest will not provide eight uninterrupted hours, and do not report until it does
Ask for an airport hotel on arrival — a 25 minute commute turns 6h50 into about 9h
Ask for the 21SEP report to be moved right by at least 1h10

conflicts.statement: Off duty 22:31Z on the 21st, report 08:35Z on the 22nd: 10h04 rest, 6h54 of sleep opportunity after the commute.
options: Notify the operator under 117.25(f) before the 22SEP report
Airport hotel on the night of the 21st
Ask for the 22SEP duty to be dropped or the report delayed — it is the second short night in a row

conflicts.statement: Off duty 17:22Z on the 25th after a 13h17 duty, report 03:25Z on the 26th: 10h03 rest, 6h53 of sleep opportunity after the commute.
options: Notify the operator under 117.25(f)
Airport hotel on the night of the 25th so the whole window is sleepable
Ask for the 26SEP report to be moved later, or for the 25SEP duty to be shortened

conflicts.statement: Off duty 13:22Z on the 26th, report 23:25Z the same evening for the FCO night duty: 10h03 rest, 6h53 of sleep opportunity, and it has to be taken in the afternoon.
options: Notify the operator under 117.25(f)
Airport hotel for the afternoon sleep, which buys back about 2h10
Ask for the 26SEP day duty or the 27SEP night duty to come off — one crew member should not fly both

conflicts.statement: Four rest periods at base fall short of the company's 12 hours: 21SEP (10h00), 22SEP (10h04), 26SEP (10h03) and the 26/27SEP evening rest (10h03). All are at or barely above the 10h regulatory floor.
options: Raise the whole 21-27SEP block with crewing as one item rather than day by day
Ask for base hotel accommodation across the block so the commute stops eating the rest
Ask for one of the four duties to be reallocated

conflicts.statement: The 21st and 22nd each give about 6h15 of sleep, below the 7h daily target, with no room for a nap because the duties run 12h11 and 9h34.
options: Accept the shortfall and protect the long recovery night on 22/23SEP as planned
Take the airport hotel option to convert the commute time into sleep
Call in fatigued if the debt has already built through the SIN pairing

conflicts.statement: 25/26SEP gives 6h05 and 26/27SEP gives 6h05 — both only just clear the 6h main-sleep floor, and 26/27 has to be taken in the afternoon before a night duty, which typically returns less than it looks.
options: Protect the 15:15Z afternoon sleep on the 26th as an actual night: blackout, phone off, household warned
Airport hotel on the 25th and 26th
Ask for the 27SEP night duty to be reallocated

conflicts.statement: 24, 25, 26 and 27SEP all report before 06:00 local (05:40, 05:05, 04:25 and 00:25). That is four in a row against a company limit of three.
options: Ask crewing to move the 27SEP FCO night duty out of the run
Ask for the 24SEP FRA turn to come off the front of the run instead
If neither moves, flag it as a fatigue risk in writing before the block starts
